name: Café Chelsea
take: French bistro classics served all day inside the Hotel Chelsea, mirrored walls, tightly set tables, and an omelet menu that runs from breakfast straight through last call.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from cafechelseanyc.com, hotelchelsea.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; walk-ins welcome daily, bar seating is first-come, first-served.
• Opened in 2022 as part of the Hotel Chelsea's reopening
• All-day French bistro menu: steak frites, maitake au poivre, pain perdu, omelets served morning through night
• Art Deco dining rooms hung with pieces from the hotel's art collection
• Popular for brunch and for people-watching from the mirrored bar area
• Has private event spaces (a wine room and a bar area) for up to about 60
• Open 7am, closing at 11pm Sunday-Wednesday and midnight Thursday-Saturday

name: Cookshop
take: Chelsea's long-running farm-to-table standby: stone-oven pizzas, a spit-roasted chicken, and a dining room that fills fastest for weekend brunch and the sidewalk tables outside.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from opentable.com, resy.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; weekends and brunch get busy, but same-week tables are usually findable.
• Opened in 2005 by chef Marc Meyer and partner Vicki Freeman.
• An early adopter of naming its farms and suppliers on a chalkboard by the door.
• Known for stone-oven pizzas, spit-roasted chicken, and a heavily attended weekend brunch.
• Has a sizeable outdoor seating section along 10th Avenue.
• Long regarded as one of Chelsea's most dependable everyday restaurants.

name: El Quijote
take: A century-old Spanish dining room inside the Hotel Chelsea, murals of Don Quixote overhead, serving garlic shrimp, patatas bravas, and a paella meant for the table.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from elquijotenyc.com, en.wikipedia.org, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy or OpenTable; bar seats make walk-ins a realistic option most nights.
• Open since 1930, now the oldest running Spanish restaurant in New York City
• Sits inside the Hotel Chelsea, sold along with the hotel in 2014
• Closed for renovation in 2018 and reopened in 2022, preserving its Don Quixote murals and sandblasted-glass artwork
• Historically a hangout for Andy Warhol, William S. Burroughs, and Janis Joplin
• Known for paella, patatas bravas, gambas al ajillo, and a Basque cheesecake
• Open 5pm to 11pm Sunday-Thursday, 5pm to midnight Friday-Saturday

name: Los Mariscos
take: A Baja-style seafood counter inside Chelsea Market: fish and shrimp tacos on handmade tortillas, ceviche by the cup, eaten fast at shared picnic tables.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from biteofthebest.com, chelseamarket.com, losmariscos.shop, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-in only, food hall counter — no reservations taken
• Baja/Tijuana-style seafood counter inside Chelsea Market's main concourse
• Known for fish and shrimp tacos on handmade tortillas, ceviche, and aguachile
• Counter service with picnic tables and a small bar pouring margaritas
• Tacos priced under $6 each
• Gets crowded at peak lunch and dinner hours

name: Pastis
take: A big, mirrored French brasserie rebuilt from the 90s original: steak frites, escargot, and trout amandine, served at a volume built for people-watching and mirror selfies.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from michelin.com, nyctourism.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; a big room makes walk-ins and bar seats a decent bet.
• Opened in 1999 by Keith McNally in the Meatpacking District, closed in 2014
• Reopened in summer 2019 one block away at 52 Gansevoort St, an $8 million rebuild with Stephen Starr as a partner
• Recreates the original's curved zinc bar, subway tile, and vintage mirrors
• Known for steak frites, escargot, trout amandine, and a double-patty cheeseburger
• Outdoor seating available
• Large, high-energy room aimed at groups and people-watching

name: Shukette
take: Mediterranean small plates built for sharing in a loud Chelsea room: warm frena bread, whole grilled fish, and lamb meatballs meant for a table of four or more.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from resy.com, shukette.org, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy, released 30 days out and gone within the hour; 20+ seats held nightly for walk-ins, expect a wait.
• Sister restaurant to Shuka in SoHo
• Levantine/Mediterranean sharing menu: frena and lafa breads, whole fish grilled in a wire cage, joojeh chicken, tahini soft serve
• Resy reservations release 30 days out and are typically gone within the first hour
• Waitlist reportedly runs into the thousands on weekend nights
• 20 to 60 seats are held each night specifically for walk-ins, with waits from 20 minutes to about 90
• Open Monday-Saturday 5pm-11pm, Sunday 4pm-10pm

name: Bar Primi
take: A pasta-forward Italian spot on the Bowery built for groups: no reservations, fast-turning tables, and a run of housemade noodles anchored by a slow-cooked lamb bucatini.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from barprimi.com, nyctourism.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Historically walk-in only, no reservations; the location is currently closed so nothing is bookable.
• Opened in 2014 by chef Andrew Carmellini's restaurant group as a casual, pasta-focused Italian spot on the Bowery.
• Known for housemade pasta specials, including a slow-cooked lamb bucatini and Thursday-night lamb chops.
• Historically took no reservations, relying on quick table turns across a two-level dining room.
• As of late September 2026, the restaurant's own site and NYC's tourism site list the Bowery location as temporarily closed for renovations, with no reopening date given.
• The same ownership group has since opened a separate Bar Primi location in the Penn District.
Temporarily closed for renovations as of September 2026 (the Penn District location is open). Bring it back from Studio → Places when the Bowery reopens.

name: Bungalow
take: East Village Indian dressed like a vintage social club: chandeliers, pink walls, a thumping playlist, and lamb chops nearly every table orders.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from bungalowny.com, en.wikipedia.org, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy opens 20 days ahead at 11am; walk-ins possible at the 8-seat bar, best early on weekdays
• Opened 2024 by chef Vikas Khanna and restaurateur Jimmy Rizvi
• Interior styled after vintage Indian social clubs, designed by Shaila Rizvi
• Given three stars by the New York Times and listed in the Michelin Guide since June 2024
• Known for Ammi's Lamb Chops, Anarkali Chicken, and slow-cooked Rajasthani lamb
• Parties of 8 or more need 40-45 days' notice

name: Claud
take: European bistro in the East Village made to feel like an apartment dinner party: razor clams, agnolotti in brown butter, and a chocolate cake meant for two.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from claudnyc.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy opens 14 days ahead at 9am; parties capped at 6, no walk-in bar
• Opened by partners Chase Sinzer and Joshua Pinsky
• Listed in the Michelin Guide
• Known for a chocolate cake for two, chicken liver agnolotti, and razor clams
• Small East Village storefront with an open kitchen counter
• Cancellations inside 24 hours are charged a fee

name: Lil' Frankie's
take: East Village red-sauce spot for wood-fired pizza and pasta, cash only, loud enough for a big table and open past 2am on weekends.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from lilfrankies.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Reservations via the restaurant's site; mostly a walk-in room, cash only
• Neapolitan-style wood-fired pizza and pasta in the East Village
• Cash only, no cards accepted
• Part of the same small local group as Frank and Supper
• Known for whole roasted eggplant, handmade gnocchi, and Margherita pizza
• Open until 2am on weeknights and 4am on weekends

name: Lucien
take: First Avenue French bistro that hasn't updated its look since 1998, steak au poivre and cramped little tables that fill up loud after dark.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, luciennyc.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Now listed on OpenTable, though it has long run on phone calls and a notebook behind the bar; call ahead to be safe.
• Opened in 1998 by Lucien Bahaj; now run by his son Zac.
• Known for steak au poivre, steak tartare, and pâté maison.
• Small, worn-in room long associated with downtown artists, photographers, and models.
• Founder Lucien Bahaj died in 2019.
• Room fills in and gets louder after about 7pm.

name: Superiority Burger
take: Plant-forward diner styled like an old East Village luncheonette: a veggie burger that falls apart on purpose and a vegan cheesesteak regulars order on repeat.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, superiorityburger.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; walk-ins welcome, especially at the back bar
• Opened in 2015 by chef Brooks Headley
• Moved in 2023 to a larger space at 119 Avenue A, the former Odessa Diner
• The New York Times gave it three stars after the move
• 2024 James Beard Outstanding Restaurant semifinalist
• Known for its namesake veggie burger and the Philadelphia Yuba sandwich

name: Veselka
take: Ukrainian diner on Second Avenue since the 1950s: pierogi, borscht, and a counter as full at midnight as it is at brunch.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, veselka.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-in only, first-come first-served; parties of 8+ can email ahead
• Opened in 1954 by Ukrainian immigrants Wolodymyr and Olha Darmochwal
• Still family-run, now by the Birchard family
• Makes thousands of pierogi and large batches of borscht daily
• Traffic roughly doubled after the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, as it became a community gathering point
• A second location opened inside Grand Central Terminal in 2023
• Scaled back from round-the-clock hours; still runs latest on weekends

name: Bernie's
take: A retro American tavern playing at a 1980s living room: dirty martinis, mozzarella sticks, crayons on the butcher paper, and a wait that gets long on weekends.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from berniesnyc.com, nyctourism.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Tock; weekend tables can mean a long wait without one, weekday bar seats are easier.
• Opened in spring 2018 by Greenpoint residents Zach Frankel and Taylor McEwan.
• Kitchen run by the team behind nearby Frankel's Delicatessen & Appetizing.
• About 50 seats, styled like a vintage American luncheonette.
• Known for dirty martinis, mozzarella sticks, and a cheeseburger deluxe.
• Gained wide attention on TikTok through servers nicknamed Marty and Missy.

name: Chez Ma Tante
take: A white-walled neighborhood bistro doing simple European classics — roast chicken, thick fries, pork shoulder — plus a Saturday brunch worth setting an alarm for.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from chezmatantebk.com, greenpointers.com, resy.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; bar seating available for walk-ins
• Opened 2017 in Greenpoint by chefs/co-owners Aidan O'Neal and Jake Leiber
• Earned two stars from the New York Times
• Menu of European bistro classics: roast chicken, pork shoulder, thick-cut fries
• Closed for building repairs in 2023, reopened summer 2024
• Serves a Saturday brunch, including its pancakes
• A long wood bar plus a few tables outside

name: El Pingüino
take: A Spanish seafood bar the size of a good living room: oysters, tinned fish, and martinis, packed into tiny wooden booths with a penguin watching over the bar.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from ilanakohn.com, pinguinogreenpoint.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; bar seats open for walk-ins
• Opened 2022 in Greenpoint by chef Nick Padilla with Mike Zorman
• Spanish seafood and cocktail bar: oysters, tinned fish, seafood towers
• Daily happy hour 4-7pm with half-price oysters and $12 martinis
• Small room with tiny wooden booths and design-forward decor
• Open daily 4pm to midnight

name: Karczma
take: Greenpoint's long-running Polish spot: a barn-style dining room, plates of pierogi and kielbasa, and a hunter's stew regulars order without opening the menu.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from greenpointers.com, karczmabrooklyn.com, opentable.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: No online booking; phone or walk-in, tables are usually easy to get
• Family-run Polish restaurant on Greenpoint Ave open for close to two decades
• Owner Slawek Letowski also opened Retro Polish Restaurant & Wine Bar in the former Christina's space in 2025
• Known for pierogi, kielbasa, white borscht in a bread bowl, and hunter's stew
• Rustic, barn-like decor with servers in traditional Polish dress
• No online reservations; phone or walk-in only
• Indoor and outdoor seating available

name: Oxomoco
take: Wood-fired Mexican in a bright, plant-filled Greenpoint room, built around oversized round booths, a chef's counter facing the grill, and tortilla-sized tlayudas.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, greenpointers.com, oxomoconyc.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; book ahead, especially weekends. Some walk-in seats at the counter and front patio.
• Opened June 2018 by the team behind Speedy Romeo pizza.
• Holds one Michelin star for wood-fired Mexican cooking.
• Known for tlayudas and a wood-grilled half chicken with housemade tortillas.
• A summer 2025 kitchen fire closed it briefly; it reopened in late July 2025 with a more seafood-leaning menu.
• Big round booths and a chef's counter facing the wood grill.

name: Wenwen
take: A loud, bright Taiwanese room in Greenpoint built around a slow-cooked beef noodle soup and hot-honey popcorn chicken, with a cocktail list as loud as the room.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, michelin.com, opentable.com, wenwenbrooklyn.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable; book ahead, the room fills fast and walk-in waits are common
• Opened February 2022 by Eric Sze and Andy Chuang, the team behind the East Village's 886
• Name combines Sze's mother Wenchi and wife Wenhui
• A New York Times Critic's Pick and listed in the Michelin Guide
• Known for a 16-hour oxtail beef noodle soup and hot-honey popcorn chicken
• Two floors: a main dining room and a lower-level space called the Alley
• 886, the sister restaurant in the East Village, closed in September 2026, but Wenwen is unaffected

name: Đi Ăn Đi
take: A plant-filled, sun-bright Vietnamese room in Greenpoint, loud at dinner, built around a beef pho ha noi and a rice-crust riff the kitchen calls its Vietnamese pizza.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from diandi.nyc, greenpointers.com, opentable.com, theinfatuation.com, timeout.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable; recommended for dinner, bar seats open to walk-ins
• Opened in 2018 by chef Dennis Ngo after roughly 13 years cooking around the city
• Name translates loosely to 'let's go eat,' a casual phrase among friends and family
• Known for beef pho ha noi, banh xeo, and a crispy rice-crust dish billed as Vietnamese pizza
• Plant-filled, pastel dining room with skylights and an open kitchen
• Recognized in the Michelin Guide
• Automatic 20% gratuity added for parties of six or more

name: Bacaro
take: Venetian small plates in a hushed, candlelit basement of brick arches, built for a slow night of cicchetti and a second bottle of wine.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from opentable.com, theinfatuation.com, thelodownny.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Not bookable through Resy or OpenTable; call the restaurant or walk in and expect a wait at peak times.
• Opened around 2007 on Division Street, at the edge of the Lower East Side and Chinatown.
• Menu is cicchetti-style, Venetian small plates meant for sharing across several dishes per couple.
• Main room is a candlelit basement with brick arches and communal farm tables.
• Not on the OpenTable or Resy booking networks as of this writing.
• Reviewers describe it as stronger on atmosphere and wine list than on kitchen consistency.

name: Cervo's
take: Iberian seafood off Canal Street: a raw bar, fried shrimp heads, and a piri piri half-chicken in a sceney Dimes Square room that fills with a well-dressed downtown crowd.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from cervosnyc.com, michelin.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy, typically booked about a week out; walk-ins have a shot early in the evening at the bar.
• Opened in 2019 from the chefs behind Wildair and Contra, part of the same downtown restaurant group.
• Known for a raw bar, fried shrimp heads, and a wood-grilled piri piri half chicken.
• Has a skylit back dining room, a bar counter, and a patio facing the Dimes Square corner.
• Rated a 'Best of the Best' 9.0 by The Infatuation and included in the Michelin Guide.
• Open for dinner only, nightly from 5:30 to 11pm.

name: Freemans
take: American tavern food down a hidden alley off the Bowery, taxidermy on the walls since 2004, mussels and artichoke dip built for a long weekend brunch.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from freemansrestaurant.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy up to 14 days out; walk-ins seated first-come first-served, larger groups by email
• Opened in 2004 down Freeman Alley off Rivington Street
• Hunting-lodge decor, including taxidermy, largely unchanged since opening
• Known for mussels in paprika butter broth, hot artichoke dip, and duck confit
• Weekend brunch adds French toast and chilaquiles
• Easier to get a table now than during its original run of hype

name: Kiki's
take: An unmarked Chinatown room serving straightforward Greek food, grilled octopus, saganaki, lamb chops, at prices that stay reasonable while a young, dressed-up crowd packs in for long waits.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from kikisnyc.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-ins welcome; reservations recommended for groups of four or more. Waits of an hour or longer are common at peak times.
• A Greek restaurant on Division Street with no exterior sign, set inside a former print shop.
• Known for grilled octopus, saganaki, lamb chops, and a horiatiki salad heavy on feta.
• Considered relatively affordable for the area, with lamb chops listed under thirty dollars.
• Draws a young, style-conscious downtown crowd, especially in the evenings.
• Open daily from noon; walk-ins are standard, with reservations suggested for parties of four or more.

name: Scarr's Pizza
take: A slice shop that mills its own flour in the basement: thin, well-charred pizza, a line out front, and an outdoor bar serving frozen drinks past midnight.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, scarrspizza.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-in only, counter service; no reservations taken.
• Opened in 2016 by Scarr Pimentel, who trained at Lombardi's.
• Mills part of its own flour on site, unusual for a slice shop.
• Moved across the street into a bigger space at 35 Orchard St in 2023.
• Repeatedly named among the city's best slices by the New York Times and The New Yorker.
• Pizza by the slice or whole pie, plus an outdoor bar serving cocktails.

name: Wildair
take: A narrow Orchard Street wine bar built around natural wine by the glass and a few small plates, beef tartare above all, in a room that stays loud and close.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from theinfatuation.com, tripadvisor.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable; walk-ins usually available at tables and the bar
• Opened around 2015 by the team behind Contra
• One of the early natural wine bars credited with popularizing the format in New York
• Known for beef tartare, bonito crudo, and stuffed olives with country ham
• Small storefront room with counter and table seating
• Closed Sundays and Mondays

name: Wu's Wonton King
take: Cantonese banquet room on East Broadway built for big round tables: whole roasted suckling pig by advance order, family-style wonton soup, and bring your own beer.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from theinfatuation.com, thelodownny.com, wuswontonkingnewyork.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Call ahead for parties of 5+; walk-ins fine otherwise, BYOB
• Family-owned Cantonese restaurant on East Broadway
• Known for whole roasted suckling pig (advance order), roasted duck, and family-style wonton soup
• BYOB with no corkage charge
• Ownership unchanged after a well-known front-of-house manager left in 2026
• Lease runs through 2027

name: 2nd Ave Deli
take: A Kips Bay deli running since the 1950s, pastrami sliced thin and served fast, matzo ball soup, and pickles on the table before anyone orders.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from 2ndavedeli.com, en.wikipedia.org, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-in only, no reservations; expect a short line at peak lunch
• Jewish deli founded in 1954 by Abe Lebewohl, originally in the East Village
• Moved to its current Kips Bay location in December 2007; now run by his nephew Jeremy Lebewohl
• Kosher, dairy-free kitchen known for pastrami, matzo ball soup, and franks in blankets
• Complimentary pickles and slaw arrive at the table before ordering
• James Beard Foundation America's Classic award, 1998

name: Casa Mono
take: A tight, small Spanish tapas room on Irving Place from chef Andy Nusser, one Michelin star, whole-animal butchery, and a wine list built entirely around Spain.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, michelin.com, opentable.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; book ahead for the dining room, walk-in tapas and wine next door at Bar Jamón
• Spanish tapas restaurant on Irving Place from chef Andy Nusser, open since 2003
• Holds one Michelin star in the current guide
• All-Spanish wine list and in-house whole-animal butchery
• Known for eggs scrambled with sea urchin and razor clams cooked a la plancha
• Small, tightly packed dining room; sister bar Bar Jamón sits next door for walk-in tapas

name: Nonna Dora's
take: A pasta-only counter in Kips Bay where a nonna in her nineties hand-rolls every noodle that morning: lasagna and casoncelli served course by course to a room built for two.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from nonnadoras.com, opentable.com, theinfatuation.com, timeout.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; book ahead, the small room fills up
• Pasta-focused bar run by Addolorata 'Dora' Marzovilla, who hand-rolls the dough herself each morning
• Kips Bay location serves only handmade pasta courses, no meat or fish mains
• Menu runs prix fixe and a five-course tasting format
• Known for a meat-and-bechamel lasagna, beet-filled casoncelli, and a rotating grano arso pasta
• Drink list built around eight negroni variations
• Marzovilla, in her nineties, opened a second location in Tribeca in 2025

name: Pongal
take: South Indian vegetarian on Curry Hill's restaurant row: crackling dosas, a wall of thalis, and a kosher kitchen that has run the room since the 1990s.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from pongalnyc.com, theinfatuation.com, tripadvisor.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-in only; no online booking, easy most nights, call ahead for large groups
• South Indian vegetarian restaurant on Lexington Ave in Curry Hill, open since 1996
• Kosher-certified kitchen, fully vegetarian with vegan and Jain-friendly options
• Known for dosas, uttapams, and thali platters, plus a dozen-plus chaat options
• Casual, no-frills room with booth seating and a small sidewalk section
• Sits among a cluster of South Asian grocers and restaurants that give Curry Hill its name

name: Tara Rose
take: A Murray Hill cocktail bar built for weekend bottomless brunch: chicken and waffles, a dining room with a working fireplace, and an outdoor bar that fills with the after-work crowd.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from hoodline.com, tararosenyc.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy for weekend bottomless brunch; walk-in any day for the a la carte menu
• Cocktail bar and kitchen in Murray Hill, opened August 2019
• Weekend bottomless brunch runs $29.95 per person over a 90-minute seating and requires the whole table to opt in
• A la carte brunch, including chicken and waffles and a lox plate, served daily without reservations
• Multiple rooms: front and back bar areas, a dining room with a working fireplace, an outdoor bar, and a bookable private speakeasy
• Reservations handled through Resy, mainly needed for the weekend bottomless seating

name: Balthazar
take: A big, loud French brasserie that runs from bacon-and-eggs breakfast through midnight steak frites, filled with SoHo regulars and out-of-towners taking photos.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from balthazarny.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy for tables; walk-in bar seats are usually doable before 7pm or after 9pm.
• Opened in 1997 by Keith McNally; still one of SoHo's most recognized dining rooms.
• Serves breakfast through dinner every day, plus weekend brunch, with its own bakery next door.
• Known for steak frites, French onion soup, a raw bar, and fresh-baked bread.
• Carries a Michelin Guide Recommended listing.
• Walk-in bar seating exists outside peak hours; dining room tables need a booking.

name: Emilio's Ballato
address: 55 E Houston St, New York, NY 10012
take: A tiny, no-reservations Italian kitchen running since 1956: red sauce, off-menu specials whispered at the table, and a line outside most nights.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from ballatos.com, michelin.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-in only, no reservations; waits of an hour or more are common, especially weekends.
• Family-run Italian kitchen at 55 E Houston St since 1956.
• No reservations; waits of an hour or more are routine, especially on weekends.
• Known for an off-menu vitello dish and old-school red-sauce staples like chicken parm.
• Long a low-key celebrity haunt without a doorman or velvet rope.
• Two rooms: a small front room for couples and a windowless back room used mostly for groups.

name: La Esquina
take: A taco counter up top, a dim and hard-to-book brasserie underneath: Mexican food running late on tequila, DJs, and a crowd that came to stay.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from esquinanyc.com, nyctourism.com, opentable.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy for the downstairs brasserie, often booked weeks out; the street-level taqueria is walk-in.
• Opened in 2005 near Lafayette and Kenmare, an early example of a NYC restaurant hiding a room downstairs.
• Three parts under one roof: a walk-up taqueria, a diner-style cafe, and a reservation-only basement brasserie.
• The underground brasserie is the harder table; the street-level taqueria is walk-in.
• DJs play most nights, and the room runs later than a typical dinner spot.
• The concept has since opened outposts in Midtown, the Upper East Side, and Moynihan Train Hall.

name: Raoul's
take: A Prince Street bistro since 1975, dim and cluttered with old art, where steak au poivre and a bar-only burger pull a late, dressed-up crowd.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from raouls.com, resy.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy, and genuinely hard to land for the dining room; the walk-in bar (with its limited burger au poivre) is the workaround.
• Open since 1975, one of SoHo's oldest continuously running restaurants.
• French bistro menu built around steak au poivre, foie gras, and Dover sole.
• The bar-only burger au poivre is a running draw, served in limited quantity each night.
• Décor includes vintage oil paintings and a taxidermied stag; a fish tank separates the front and back rooms.
• Weekend brunch runs 11am-2:30pm; dinner is served every night, with the bar opening at 5pm.

name: Rubirosa
take: Family-run red-sauce Italian since 2009: thin-crust pies, a swirled vodka-and-pesto pizza everyone orders, and a packed, easygoing room that still feels like old Mulberry Street.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from resy.com, rubirosanyc.com, timeout.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy books up, but roughly half the room is held back for walk-ins.
• Opened in 2009 by the Pappalardo family, who also ran Joe & Pat's Pizzeria on Staten Island.
• Best known for a thin-crust vodka pizza and a tableside 'tie-dye' pie swirling pesto into the sauce.
• 87 seats, with roughly half held for walk-ins rather than reservations.
• Founder Angelo 'AJ' Pappalardo died in 2015; his sister Maria now runs the restaurant.
• Runs an extensive gluten-free menu, including a gluten-free vodka pie.

name: Thai Diner
take: A Thai-accented diner in Nolita mixing khao soi and wok noodles with disco fries and Thai tea French toast, bamboo-lined booths, and a crowd running from neighbors to weekend tourists.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from michelin.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy for dinner; brunch and weekends usually mean a wait for walk-ins.
• Opened in 2020 by chefs Ann Redding and Matt Danzer, following their earlier restaurant Uncle Boons.
• Menu combines Thai dishes like khao soi with diner staples reworked using Thai ingredients.
• Known for Thai tea French toast, a Thai-spiced take on disco fries, and an egg sandwich on roti.
• Holds a Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand distinction.
• Reservations run through Resy; the room stays busy most of the day, especially at brunch.

name: Chambers
take: A Tribeca wine bar built around a serious by-the-glass list, with small plates like roast chicken and semolina bread for the sommeliers drinking at the marble counter.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from michelin.com, opentable.com, theinfatuation.com, tribecacitizen.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; book ahead - a few communal-table seats are held for walk-ins before 7pm.
• Opened in 2022 by Master Sommelier Pascaline Lepeltier, David Lillie of Chambers Street Wines, and chef Jonathan Karis
• Tiny room built around a marble bar and roughly 21 seats
• By-the-glass list runs to about 20 pours, from $10 drafts to rare $49 bottles
• Beverage program picked up a 2026 James Beard nomination
• Named to the New York Times' 100 best NYC restaurants list
• Known for roast chicken, Rhode Island squid, and fermented semolina bread

name: Estancia 460
take: A Tribeca clubhouse since the mid-90s: whitewashed brick, a mixed grill for two, and empanadas regulars order without glancing at the menu.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from estancia460.com, hobnobmag.com, opentable.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy or phone; usually easy to get in, private groups up to about 30.
• Open in Tribeca since 1995, owned by Stacey Sosa
• Argentine menu with Italian and Spanish influences: empanadas, parrillada mixed grill, milanesa napolitana, thin-crust pizzas
• Whitewashed brick walls and simple wooden tables built to feel like a ranch house
• South American-heavy wine list, plus BYO with corkage
• Weekend brunch runs 10:30am to 4pm; has a small, non-reservable patio
• Known as a neighborhood regulars' spot for downtown locals

name: Faux
take: A French bistro from Keith McNally's son, open since September: oysters and steak frites in a dim, packed room that only gets louder, plus a late-night bar downstairs.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from opentable.com, theinfatuation.com, tribecacitizen.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable; new and busy, but walk-ins are welcomed, especially at the downstairs bar.
• Opened September 2026 by George McNally, son of restaurateur Keith McNally
• Chef is Kristina Ramos, previously at Michelin-starred kitchens
• Occupies the former B Flat space between Franklin and White, with a ground-floor dining room and a downstairs late-night bar
• French coastal/bistro menu built around classics like oysters, steak, and burgers
• Downstairs bar runs Tuesday through Saturday from 7pm
• Named an OpenTable Icons pick for 2026

name: Frenchette
take: Tribeca French with real technique behind it and a menu that rewrites itself daily: duck frites, dressed-up scrambled eggs, and a dining room that gets loud by eight.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, frenchettenyc.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy/SevenRooms; the dining room books out a few weeks for prime times, bar seats are easier to walk into.
• Opened in 2018 by chefs Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson, longtime collaborators from Keith McNally's Balthazar, Pastis, and Minetta Tavern.
• Won the James Beard Award for Best New Restaurant in 2019.
• The full menu, including the wine list, changes daily rather than running fixed dishes.
• Known for duck frites with bearnaise and a brouillade of soft scrambled eggs.
• Included on Pete Wells' 2023 list of the 100 best restaurants in New York City.

name: Locanda Verde
take: Andrew Carmellini's big, easygoing Tribeca Italian: his grandmother's ravioli on the menu, a lively bar up front, and round tables built for large groups.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, locandaverdenyc.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy or OpenTable; generally gettable for most occasions.
• Chef Andrew Carmellini's Tribeca Italian, known for his grandmother's ravioli recipe.
• Large, adaptable dining room with bar seats, two-tops, and big round tables for groups.
• Serves breakfast, lunch, weekend brunch, and dinner daily.
• Artwork in the space includes pieces by Robert De Niro Sr.
• Reviewers describe it as an easier reservation now than it was at its 2009 opening.

name: Paros
take: Greek seafood in a bright white Tribeca room done up like a Cycladic villa, whole fish and grilled octopus over a thumping soundtrack aimed at big groups.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from theinfatuation.com, tribecacitizen.com, tripadvisor.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; moderately easy to book, bar seats often open for walk-ins.
• Opened October 2023 at the corner of West Broadway and Franklin
• Run by brothers George Pagonis (chef, trained at the CIA, formerly of Le Cirque and Aureole) and Nick Pagonis (front of house)
• Renovated a previously underused corner space into a bright, high-ceilinged dining room
• Known for whole fish, chargrilled octopus, and Greek dips and salads
• Open daily including lunch, 11:30am to 10pm
• Has both indoor and outdoor seating

name: The Odeon
take: A Tribeca brasserie unchanged since 1980: onion soup, burgers, and steak frites under Deco lighting, still full of downtown regulars and the occasional stray celebrity.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, theinfatuation.com, theodeonrestaurant.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable; usually gettable within the week, and the bar takes walk-ins.
• Opened in 1980 by Keith McNally, Brian McNally, and Lynn Wagenknecht in a former cafeteria space.
• Became a fixture of the 1980s downtown art and nightlife scene, name-checked in Bright Lights, Big City and shown in Saturday Night Live's opening credits.
• Bartenders here are widely credited with inventing the Cosmopolitan cocktail.
• Still owned and operated by Lynn Wagenknecht.
• Known for French onion soup, burgers, and moules frites.

name: Tiny's & the Bar Upstairs
take: New American comfort food in a pink 19th-century Tribeca townhouse: a thick burger downstairs, a tight little bar up top, and a low-key date-night hum.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from theinfatuation.com, tinysnyc.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; downstairs tables are usually gettable, the upstairs bar has only a few walk-in seats.
• Occupies a pink 1810s townhouse on West Broadway, one of the older buildings in Tribeca.
• Family run by siblings Ana, Matt, and Jack Abramcyk.
• Spread over three floors: a ground-floor dining room, a lower level, and an upstairs bar.
• Known for a thick burger on a brioche bun and a kale salad with apple and pecans.
• Offers a $150 Sunday supper set for two to four people.

name: Anton's
take: Comfort-forward American cooking with European touches in a warm, low-lit West Village room loud enough to talk privately, set inside the old Frankies 570 space.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from antonsnyc.com, theinfatuation.com, tollbit.gothamist.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; the restaurant says it holds tables for walk-in guests every night.
• Opened in November 2019 by chef-owner Nick Anderer, named for his great-great-grandfather.
• Took over the West Village corner space that had housed Frankies 570 Spuntino.
• Menu leans toward American and European comfort dishes, including housemade pastas and a hanger steak.
• Dinner runs 5-11pm Sunday through Thursday and to midnight Friday-Saturday, with weekend brunch and Friday lunch.
• Posted hours vary by source, so full weekly hours were not confirmed with confidence.

name: Boucherie West Village
take: A big, mirrored French brasserie on a Seventh Avenue corner: steak frites, escargot, and a room loud enough that no one minds ordering another round.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from boucherieus.com, nycaller.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable; recommended for dinner given the size and traffic, easier at lunch or the bar.
• Occupies the former Circle Repertory Theater building on a Seventh Avenue South corner.
• Roughly 320 seats across a main dining room, butcher counter, second-floor gallery, and outdoor café.
• Known for steak frites, escargot, and raw seafood towers.
• Dinner runs about $75-120 a person before tip.
• Open daily until midnight.

name: Buvette
take: A snug French café on a Grove Street corner, marble counters and shoulder-to-shoulder tables serving steamed eggs and coffee from morning into wine at night.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from ilovebuvette.com, nycaller.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Mostly walk-in; Resy available for brunch and prime dinner slots, but timing flexibility helps.
• Opened in 2011 by chef Jody Williams.
• Known for steamed eggs, croque madame, and all-day wine and coffee service.
• Very small room with tightly packed marble tables; not built for groups.
• Open daily from morning straight through to midnight.

name: Cowgirl
take: A Wild West-themed Texan kitchen on Hudson Street, all antler chandeliers and gingham, built for frito pie, margaritas, and a rowdy table of friends.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from cowgirlnyc.com, en.wikipedia.org, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Walk-ins generally fine; call ahead for larger parties.
• Opened in 1989 by Sherry Delamarter as Cowgirl Hall of Fame.
• Texas- and Southern-inspired comfort food: frito pie, chicken fried steak, margaritas.
• Decorated wall to wall with longhorn skulls, saddles, and western memorabilia.
• Menu includes kid-friendly items like corn dogs and mac and cheese alongside the bar scene.
• One of the longer-running restaurants in the West Village, still trading on nostalgia decades in.

name: Don Angie
take: Italian-American in a dim, leather-lined West Village room built for two, known for garlicky stuffed flatbread and a spiral lasagna made to share.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from donangie.com, en.wikipedia.org, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable, released seven days ahead at 9am; bar seats go to walk-ins, typically about an hour wait.
• Opened in 2017 by chefs Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli.
• Earned a Michelin star in 2021 and lost it in 2023.
• Known for a pinwheel lasagna made for two and stuffed garlic flatbread.
• Small leather-and-mirror room best suited to couples and small groups.
• Weekend lunch service runs Friday through Sunday in addition to nightly dinner.

name: Emmett's on Grove
take: Chicago-style tavern pizza in a half-sunken, wood-paneled Grove Street room, thin-crust pies built for splitting alongside ribs and a long wine list.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from emmettsongrove.com, timeout.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Online through the restaurant's site or by phone; bar seats workable for walk-ins.
• Opened by Chicago native Emmett Burke, who also runs Emmett's pizzeria in Soho.
• Known for Chicago tavern-style thin-crust pizza cut into squares.
• Menu also covers baby back ribs and chicken parmesan.
• Half-below-sidewalk-level room styled like a Midwest supper club.
• Weekend brunch service and a kitchen open past midnight Friday and Saturday.

name: Jeffrey's Grocery
take: A corner seafood spot in the West Village built around a raw bar and a clam chowder regulars keep reordering, unhurried from weekday lunch straight through late dinner.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from jeffreysgrocery.com, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: OpenTable; walk-ins are usually fine outside peak weekend brunch hours.
• A West Village corner restaurant centered on a raw bar and an all-day seafood menu.
• Started as a small grocery-and-cafe concept before dropping the market side to focus on full dining.
• Clam chowder and raw-bar oysters are the most consistently mentioned order.
• Runs lunch, an oyster happy hour, and dinner on weekdays, plus weekend brunch starting at 10am.
• Reservations are taken through OpenTable, with short waits reported at peak brunch times.

name: L'Artusi
take: A West Village pasta room open since 2008: short-ingredient-list noodles that land more complex than they read, a loud front bar, and a stacked-up crowd most nights by early evening.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from lartusi.com, theinfatuation.com, tripadvisor.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy, released two weeks out at 9am; bar and counter seats are held for walk-ins.
• Opened in 2008 by sommelier Joe Campanale and chef Gabe Thompson as a follow-up to dell'anima.
• Known for pastas built from short ingredient lists, including a widely ordered chili-and-breadcrumb spaghetti.
• Weekend brunch at the bar draws an especially loud, spritz-heavy crowd.
• Dinner runs to midnight on Friday and Saturday; the dining room fills early most nights.
• Rated 8.5 out of 10 by The Infatuation as of its most recent review update.

name: Minetta Tavern
take: A Village standby built around a dry-aged burger, red leather booths, caricatures of old regulars on the walls, and a bar that's three deep most nights.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, minettatavernny.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy or phone; book ahead. Bar seating sometimes open to walk-ins.
• Building operated as a tavern from 1937; Keith McNally reopened it as a French bistro in 2009.
• Known for the dry-aged Black Label Burger and a côte de boeuf for two.
• Held a Michelin star from 2010 to 2018.
• Red banquettes lined with caricatures of longtime regulars.
• A second location opened in Washington, D.C. in December 2024.

name: Via Carota
take: A tiny, candlelit West Village trattoria built around vegetables and a cacio e pepe half the room orders, usually with a line trailing down Grove Street.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, theinfatuation.com, viacarota.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Mostly walk-in only; a handful of Resy tables exist, but most nights mean a wait of one to three hours with no bar shortcut.
• Opened November 2014 by Jody Williams and Rita Sodi, who also run I Sodi and Buvette.
• Both chefs received James Beard Foundation 'Best Chef: NYC' honors in 2019.
• Known for cacio e pepe tonarelli, a chopped-steak svizzerina, and an unusually long list of vegetable dishes.
• Runs a small dining room where most tables go to walk-ins rather than reservations.
• Has appeared repeatedly on the New York Times' annual list of the city's best restaurants.

name: Birds of a Feather
take: Sichuan cooking from the Cafe China team in a bright, minimal room built around one long communal table, heavy on chili oil and mouth-numbing heat.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from birdsofafeatherny.com, theinfatuation.com, tollbit.gothamist.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; usually gettable outside peak weekend dinner
• Opened 2017 in Williamsburg by the team behind Michelin-starred Cafe China
• Sichuan menu built on chili oil and numbing spice
• Known for dishes like poached wontons in chili sauce and dan dan noodles
• Bright, minimal room centered on a communal table, geared toward groups
• Most dishes run under $20

name: Diner
take: A vintage dining car under the Williamsburg Bridge, running since 1998: thick burgers, daily specials scrawled on butcher paper, and barely enough room to pass the ketchup.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from dinernyc.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy recommended given the small room; walk-ins possible off-peak.
• Opened New Year's Eve 1998 in a vintage Kullman dining car under the Williamsburg Bridge.
• Founded by Andrew Tarlow and Mark Firth, early figures in Williamsburg's restaurant scene.
• Known for a thick burger, brisket and eggs, and daily specials written on butcher paper at the table.
• Marked 25 years in business in 2023 and remains open.
• Under the same ownership group as the nearby Marlow & Daughters butcher shop.

name: Fish Cheeks
take: Thai seafood built around coconut crab curry and whole fried fish, split between a loud bar up front and a quieter wedge-shaped room in back.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from fishcheeksnyc.com, forbes.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy, recommended — it's new and busy; some seats at the front bar for walk-ins
• Opened May 2025 as a second location of the NoHo original, which dates to 2016
• Run by chef Dustin Everett under 55 Hospitality
• Known for coconut crab curry, whole fried fish, and Zaab wings
• Deliberately skips Americanized Thai staples like pad thai
• Two rooms: a busy front bar and a smaller back room
• Daily happy hour from noon to 6pm

name: Kellogg's Diner
take: A century-old diner rebuilt with a Texas accent: chrome booths, flat nachos and Tex-Mex enchiladas alongside French toast, open around the clock.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from bkmag.com, kelloggsdinernyc.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy available, but it's a 24-hour diner — walk in anytime
• Nearly century-old Williamsburg diner that closed in a 2023 bankruptcy
• Reopened in 2024 under restaurateur Louis Skibar with chef Jackie Carnesi, formerly of Nura
• Reworked into a Tex-Mex-leaning diner: flat nachos, enchiladas, Texas French toast
• Now operates 24 hours a day
• Classic chrome-and-booth diner interior, renovated during the relaunch

name: Laser Wolf
take: An Israeli grill house on the Hoxton's rooftop: skewers off the charcoal fire, a dozen little salatim to start, and a Manhattan skyline behind every table.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from michelin.com, thehoxton.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy, popular and best booked ahead; walk-ins possible at the bar
• Israeli grill from chef Michael Solomonov's CookNSolo, part of Boka Restaurant Group
• Sits on the rooftop of the Hoxton hotel in Williamsburg with Manhattan skyline views
• Known for charcoal-grilled skewers, a spread of salatim mezze, and whole branzino
• Kitchen runs until 1am Thursday through Saturday
• A Michelin Guide-listed restaurant

name: Lilia
take: Missy Robbins' bright, wood-fired Italian in a former Williamsburg auto-body shop: sheep's milk agnolotti, wood-grilled seafood, and a dressed-up crowd that books weeks out for a table.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from bkmag.com, lilianewyork.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy and phone (phone lines open 30 days out at 10am, online at midnight); bar seats are walk-in but typically mean a wait.
• Opened in 2016 by chef Missy Robbins in a converted former auto-body shop.
• Sister restaurant to Misi, also in Williamsburg.
• Known for sheep's milk agnolotti and wood-grilled seafood.
• Historically one of the hardest reservations in New York; phone and online booking windows open on staggered schedules.
• Bar seats are available to walk-ins, usually with a wait of about two hours.

name: Llama Inn
take: Peruvian small plates on a plant-covered Williamsburg patio: ceviche, lomo saltado, and pisco cocktails that traded formal dining for a laid-back backyard mood before closing at the end of 2025.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from en.wikipedia.org, greenpointers.com, theinfatuation.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Formerly booked through Resy; the restaurant has closed permanently.
• Opened in November 2015, among the first contemporary Peruvian restaurants in Williamsburg.
• Michelin-listed and included in New York Magazine's 'The Thousand Best.'
• Renovated in 2021 into a more casual space with a heated outdoor cabana patio.
• Closed permanently at the end of 2025 after a decade in business.
• The space is set to reopen in spring 2026 as Cafe Bar J.F., a South American tavern from the same ownership group.
Closed for good at the end of 2025 after ten years; a café is slated for the space. Kept for the record.

name: St. Anselm
take: A tight, wood-fired steakhouse that's been a Williamsburg fixture since 2010: an open kitchen, a short bar, and a hanger steak regulars order without looking at the menu.
notes:
— Sep 23, 2026 · ROUND desk
Researched from greenpointers.com, stanselm.net, theinfatuation.com, yelp.com; written in ROUND's words.
Reservations: Resy; prime-time dinner is hard to land, walk-ins seated first-come as space allows
• Opened in 2010, one of Williamsburg's earlier modern steakhouses
• Known for open-fire cooking and its hanger 'butcher's steak'
• Closed temporarily after a fire, reopened in February 2025
• Small room: roughly eight tables plus counter seats facing the open kitchen
• Extensive wine list alongside the steak-focused menu
